{{Short description|Czech mathematician (1926–2022)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2022}}
'''Jaroslav Kurzweil''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈjaroslaf ˈkurtsvajl}}, 7 May 1926, [[Prague]] – 17 March 2022) was a Czech [[mathematician]].

==Biography==
Born in [[Prague]], [[First Czechoslovak Republic|Czechoslovakia]], Kurzweil was a specialist in [[ordinary differential equation]]s and defined the [[Henstock–Kurzweil integral]] in terms of [[Riemann integral|Riemann sums]], first published in 1957 in the Czechoslovak Mathematical Journal. He has been awarded the highest possible scientific prize of Czechia, the "Czech Brain" of the year 2006, as an acknowledgement of his life achievements.<ref>[http://www.radio.cz/en/news/83895 Mathematician Jaroslav Kurzweil to be awarded "Czech Brain" prize], {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717225115/http://www.radio.cz/en/news/83895|date=17 July 2010}} [[Czech Radio]], 10 May 2006. Accessed 23 January 2010</ref><ref>[http://www.math.cas.cz/about-awards.html Awards of researchers of the Institute.] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20080229234206/http://www.math.cas.cz/about-awards.html|date=29 February 2008}} Institute of Mathematics of the Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic. Accessed 23 January 2010</ref>

With limited opportunities of contact between mathematicians within the [[Iron Curtain]] and those from the West, Kurzweil and [[Ivo Babuška]] founded a series of international scientific conferences named EQUADIFF, being held every four years since 1962 alternately in Prague, [[Bratislava]], and [[Brno]]. He was chief editor of Mathematica Bohemica (then called ''Časopis pro pěstování matematiky'') from 1956 to 1970 and was in its editorial board until 2007. In 2007, Kurzweil delivered a New Year's toast on Czech Television.<ref>[http://users.math.cas.cz/~tvrdy/JK90-MathBohem_141-2016-2-1.pdf Ninety years of Jaroslav Kurzweil]</ref>
